Where is everybody? [0.3] Our galaxy should be full of aliens.
It has hundreds of billions of stars, most with planets, and it's over ten billion years old.
Even at one percent of light speed, a civilization could cross it in about ten million years.
So why has no one shown up? That's the Fermi paradox. [0.3] Here are the three best answers.
One: we're too far apart. Our radio signals have only filled a bubble about two hundred light-years wide.
Two: we've barely looked. Our searches so far are like checking one hot tub of water, out of all Earth's oceans.
Three: the Great Filter. Some step on the way to the stars is almost impossible, [0.3] and it may still be ahead of us.
Until we know which one is true, the question stays open.
